description: 2026-era incident corpus. The SmartBugs Curated benchmark is 2018-era and cannot exercise these classes, so this corpus is the instrument for them. Each detector has a POSITIVE fixture (must fire) and a CONTROL (must not). Scored by scripts/benchmark-incidents.ts: recall on positives, and cross-talk — findings on a fixture that its manifest entry does not expect, which is the false-positive measure a fixture corpus can actually make. CROSS-TALK excludes hygiene/presence notes and each case's `tolerate` list; every tolerance carries a `tolerateWhy` justification, so co-firing is either explained or it fails the gate.

cases.incident: KolanHook (Ethereum, 1.279453 ETH) — the real entry point, from the vendored PoC
cases.note: accept() is an ungated settlement entry in a hook contract; the callback itself is guarded. Added after the vendored PoC showed the name-keyed rule missed the incident.

tolerateWhy.reentrancy: accept() writes the window and then transfers, so the call-then-write window is real
tolerateWhy.timestamp: the expiry check uses block.timestamp, which the rule correctly reports
tolerateWhy.unprotected-ether: accept() pays an unguarded caller, which is true and is the same defect the detector under test describes from the hook side
